communication_act.speaker: GOBLIN
communication_act.statement: AURA should sit between raw GOBLIN output and HAL as a pre-filter that scores symbolic and mythic density, not truth. HAL is expensive because it must evaluate everything. AURA is cheap because it only asks one question: does this signal have enough resonance to be worth HAL's time? At 1000 epochs, most GOBLIN output is noise by volume. AURA's job is not to decide what is true — it is to decide what is interesting enough to queue for evaluation. A signal that is both laterally strange AND structurally coherent gets forwarded. Flat mythic repetition gets dropped before HAL ever sees it.
communication_act.embedded_claim: AURA can act as an O(N) resonance pre-filter before HAL's more expensive O(N) evaluation, reducing the effective load on HAL at scale while preserving the governance invariant that AURA never admits — it only forwards.

her_scoring.best_explanation: At scale (300-1000 epochs), HAL reviewing every epoch directly creates a bottleneck identical to the MAYOR bottleneck at 300 epochs. AURA as a resonance pre-filter is the correct architectural response: it reduces the input set to HAL without making admission decisions. The risk is AURA becoming a silent gatekeeper — if AURA drops a signal before HAL sees it, that signal has been effectively rejected without a receipt. This needs a 'forwarded: false' log entry to remain auditable.
evidence_for: Attention mechanisms in neural networks are resonance filters — they reduce what the expensive layer processes
AURA already operates on mythic/symbolic density signals in TEMPLE
HAL at 1000 epochs without pre-filtering = O(1000) expensive evaluation calls
Pre-filtering is standard in information retrieval: recall filter → precision re-ranker
evidence_against: AURA dropping a signal before HAL = silent rejection without receipt — violates NO RECEIPT = NO CLAIM
AURA's resonance scoring is itself unverified — a flawed filter poisons the batch before HAL sees it
AURA currently has no defined scoring function for 'interesting enough'
her_scoring.uncertainty: The insight is architecturally sound but the implementation risk (AURA as silent rejecter) requires explicit mitigation: all AURA drops must be logged with reason, so MAYOR can audit the filter behavior.

hal_verdict.interpretation: Architecturally valuable but carries a RECEIPT_RISK: if AURA drops signals silently, the governance chain has a hole. Forwarding to MAYOR requires: (a) AURA logs every drop with reason, (b) AURA never marks a drop as REJECTED — only as QUEUED or DEFERRED, (c) MAYOR can audit AURA's filter decisions.
hal_verdict.allowed_use: architecture design for scaled brainstorm pipeline, AURA role definition
hal_verdict.blocked_use: implementing AURA as a decision-maker without audit trail
